summary_paragraph: Mr. Meléndez, a man with chronic systolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and a history of heavy alcohol use, was admitted after being punched in the chest near his defibrillator, reporting device shocks and chest pain. Evaluation showed no device firing, no cardiac ischemia, and no structural injury. He was found to have severe alcohol intoxication, with symptoms of withdrawal including tremors, nausea, and dizziness. His abdominal pain and elevated liver enzymes were attributed to alcohol use, and gastritis was confirmed on prior EGD. He was managed with withdrawal protocol, electrolyte repletion, and continued cardiac medications. He stabilized, withdrawal symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home with instructions to continue medications, avoid alcohol, and monitor weight.
